Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And God said to Moses and Aaron, in the land of Egypt, saying:
translations.2: "This month shall be for you the first of months — it shall be for you the first of the months of the year.
translations.3: Speak to the assembly of the sons of Israel, saying: on the tenth of it, let every company take for itself a head — a head of the households of their fathers, one head for each household.
translations.4: But if the people of the household are too few for the need of a head, then let him and his neighbor who is nearest to his dwelling take one together, in equal shares among the souls — each man according to the measure of his food shall you reckon it.
translations.5: And let there be for you a head — one that is sound, a male of its year; from the sheep and the goats you shall take it.
translations.6: It shall be kept by you until the fourteenth day of this month; and the whole company of the assembly of the sons of Israel shall slaughter it between the two twilights.
translations.7: And they shall take of its blood and place it upon the two cheeks of the door and upon the lintel, upon the houses in which they shall eat it.
translations.8: And they shall eat its flesh that night — roasted over fire — and unleavened bread; with bitter herbs they shall eat it.
translations.9: Do not eat of it raw, nor cooked by boiling in water, but only roasted over fire — its head and its legs and its inner parts.
translations.10: And you shall leave nothing of it until the morning; and if anything remains of it until the morning, then burn it with fire.
translations.11: And in this manner shall you eat it: your loins girded firmly, your sandals on your feet, and your staffs in your hands; and eat it in haste — it is the Passover unto God.
translations.12: For I shall appear in the land of Egypt that night, and I shall slay every firstborn within it, from human to beast; and upon all the objects of worship of the Egyptians I shall execute judgments — I am God, the One.
translations.13: And the blood shall be for you a sign upon the houses in which you are — I shall look upon it and have compassion for you, and no lethal pestilence shall befall you, when I strike the people of the land of Egypt.
translations.14: And this day shall be for you a memorial — you shall celebrate it as a festival unto God, for your generations; it is an ordinance forever that you shall celebrate it.
translations.15: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; but on the first day you shall remove the leavening agent from your houses — for whoever eats leavened bread, that person shall be cut off from among the house of Israel, from the first day until the seventh day.
translations.16: And the first day shall be a consecrated name, and the seventh day shall be a consecrated name for you; no labor whatsoever shall be done on either of them — except only what is to be eaten for every soul, that alone may be done for you.
translations.17: And keep the unleavened bread — for on the very substance of this day I brought out your hosts from the land of Egypt; so keep this day for your generations as an ordinance forever.
translations.18: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of it at eventide, eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of it at eventide.
translations.19: Seven days — no leaven shall be found in your houses; for whoever eats anything leavened, that person shall be cut off from the assembly of the house of Israel, whether he be a stranger or a native of the land.
translations.20: Anything leavened you shall not eat; in all your dwellings eat unleavened bread.
translations.21: And Moses called for all the elders of the sons of Israel and said to them: 'Go forth and take for yourselves a flock for your clans, and slaughter the Passover.
translations.22: And take a bundle of hyssop and dip it in the blood which is in the basin, and apply it to the lintel and to the two cheeks of the door from that blood; and let no person among you go out from the door of his dwelling until the morning.
translations.23: For God shall appear to strike the Egyptians, and shall see the blood upon the lintel and the two cheeks of the door, and shall have compassion for whoever is within; and He shall not permit the destroyer to enter into your houses to bring ruin.
translations.24: And keep this matter as an ordinance for you and for your generations forever.
translations.25: And when you enter the land which God shall give you as He has promised, then keep this rite.
translations.26: And it shall be, when your children say to you: "What is this rite for you?" —
translations.27: say: "It is a slaughter of compassion unto God, for He showed compassion for the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt, when He struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses." And the people bowed down and prostrated themselves.
translations.28: And the sons of Israel went and did as God had commanded Moses and Aaron — so they did.
translations.29: And when it was at the middle of the night, God slew every firstborn in the land of Egypt — from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat upon his throne, to the firstborn of the captive who was in the prison — and all the firstborn of the beasts.
translations.30: And Pharaoh arose in the night — he and all his servants and the rest of the Egyptians — and there was a great cry in Egypt, since there was no house in which there was not a dead one.
translations.31: And he called for Moses and Aaron in the night, and said: 'Arise, go out from among my people — you two and the sons of Israel — and go forth; serve God as you have said.'
translations.32: 'Also your flocks and your herds — take them, as you have said; and go; and release me from obligation.'
translations.33: And the Egyptians pressed upon the people to hasten to send them out from the land, for they said: 'We are all dying.'
translations.34: And the people carried their dough before it had leavened; and their kneading-bowls were bound up in their garments upon their necks.
translations.35: And the sons of Israel did at that time as Moses had commanded them, and asked as gifts from the Egyptians vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments.
translations.36: And God gave the people favor before the Egyptians, and they gave these as gifts to them; and so the Egyptians were stripped.
translations.37: Then the sons of Israel journeyed from Ein Shams (Raamses) to Succoth — numbering about six hundred thousand on foot, adult men, besides the little ones.
translations.38: And also a great mixed multitude went up with them, and flocks and cattle — a very great quantity of livestock.
translations.39: And they baked the dough which they had brought out from Egypt as flat unleavened cakes, for it had not leavened — since they had been driven out from Egypt and had not been able to linger, and even provisions they had not prepared for themselves.
translations.40: And the sojourn of the sons of Israel, which they sojourned in the labors of Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years.
translations.41: And when it was after four hundred and thirty years, on the very substance of that day, all the hosts of God went out from the land of Egypt.
translations.42: And just as there had been a night of watching unto God, to bring them out from the land of Egypt, so this night is kept for the sons of Israel throughout their generations.
translations.43: Then God said to Moses and Aaron: 'This is the ordinance of the Passover — no foreigner shall eat of it.
translations.44: But every slave belonging to a man, purchased for a price — circumcise him, and then he may eat of it.
translations.45: The sojourner and the hired laborer shall not eat of it.
translations.46: In one dwelling shall it be eaten; you shall not carry out from the house any of the flesh to the outside; and a bone you shall not break of it.
translations.47: Thus shall the greater part of the assembly of the sons of Israel do it.
translations.48: And when a stranger sojourns among you and wishes to make a Passover unto God, let every male in his vicinity be circumcised — and then let him come forward to make it, for he shall become as a native of the land; but any uncircumcised person shall not eat of it.
translations.49: One law shall there be for the native and for the stranger who has entered among you.'
translations.50: And the sons of Israel did as God had commanded Moses and Aaron — so they did.
translations.51: And when it was on the very substance of that day, God brought out the sons of Israel from the land of Egypt by their hosts.
